market.question: Will WTI Crude Oil (WTI) hit (HIGH) $120 in April?

assessment.reasoning: WTI is currently trading around $94.40/barrel as of April 24-25, 2026, with the April monthly high reaching $117.63 per the Investing.com 52-week range data. The $120 threshold is approximately 27% above current price with only ~3 trading days left before April 30 resolution. The EIA STEO forecasts Brent peaking at $115/b in Q2 2026, with a Brent-WTI spread of $15/b in April — implying a WTI peak forecast of roughly $100/b, well below $120. The 52-week intraday high for WTI is $117.63, meaning $120 has NOT yet been reached in April. To resolve YES, WTI would need to surge ~$25 (~27%) from current levels in under 3 days, requiring an extreme geopolitical shock (e.g., full Strait of Hormuz closure escalation or dramatic breakdown in US-Iran talks). Diplomatic momentum toward US-Iran talks is currently dampening supply-risk premium. While the geopolitical backdrop (ongoing US naval blockade, Strait of Hormuz disruptions) provides some non-trivial tail risk, the gap to $120 from ~$94-97 in under 3 days is very large.
data_sources: Investing.com: WTI current price ~$94.40, today's range $92.68-$97.85, 52-week high $117.63
TradingEconomics: WTI slipped below $94 on April 24 on US-Iran peace talk hopes, weekly gain ~14%
EIA STEO April 2026: Brent forecast peak $115/b in Q2 2026; Brent-WTI spread peaks at $15/b in April → WTI implied peak ~$100/b
Barchart: June WTI CLM26 closed down -1.45 on April 24; Strait of Hormuz 'essentially closed'
LiteFinance: WTI April 2026 forecast range $82.72-$133.91; prior spike to $113.13 following US-Israel military action vs. Iran
assessment.key_uncertainty: A sudden, dramatic escalation in the Strait of Hormuz conflict (e.g., full closure, tanker attacks, or collapse of US-Iran talks) in the final ~3 trading days of April could drive a spike toward or past $120; conversely, a peace breakthrough would push prices sharply lower.
